chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad or another, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about what is permissible for a woman to wear while in the state of Ihram. He said: All garments, except the two gloves, the burqa' (head veil), and silk. I said: She may wear khazz (silk-like fabric). He said: Yes. I said: But its warp is ibrisam (raw silk), and it is silk. He said: As long as it is not pure silk, there is no objection.

key_terms.الْبُرُقُعَ: The burqa' (a specific type of head veil covering the face)
key_terms.الْخَزَّ: Khazz (a type of silk fabric or silk-like material)
key_terms.مُحْرِمَةٌ: A woman in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What clothing is permissible for a woman to wear while in the state of Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of silk in Ihram applies strictly to pure silk (harir), allowing mixed fabrics like khazz even if their warp is silk, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between material essence and blend. This ruling highlights the practical flexibility granted to women regarding head coverings, specifically permitting the burqa' (face veil) while prohibiting gloves, a point of discussion among scholars regarding the preservation of beauty (zina) during pilgrimage.
